skill.name: minimax-xlsx
skill.description: Create, read, edit, format, and validate Excel workbooks, CSV files, and TSV files using local OOXML-focused tools.
skill.summary: Create, edit, analyze, and validate Excel workbooks with formula and formatting checks.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from OOXML namespace strings, Markdown code spans, and expected local spreadsheet file handling. Confirmed issues are privileged LibreOffice install guidance, caller-controlled output directory deletion, and an unsafe manual unzip fallback.

remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo apt-get commands from skill docs and script output. Tell users to install LibreOffice outside the agent session.
Reject root, home, and non-temporary output directories before shutil.rmtree. Prefer a newly created mkdtemp work directory.
Delete the manual unzip fallback or require the same realpath member validation used by xlsx_unpack.py before extraction.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet edits often break formulas, styles, or workbook structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safer XLSX creation, editing, validation, and analysis.
actual_capabilities: Creates new XLSX workbooks from a minimal OOXML template.
Reads and analyzes XLSX, XLSM, CSV, and TSV data with helper scripts and pandas.
Edits existing XLSX files through unpack, XML edit, and repack workflows to preserve workbook structure.
Adds spreadsheet columns, inserts rows, and shifts affected formula references with provided scripts.
Checks formulas statically and can run LibreOffice recalculation when it is already available.
Applies financial model formatting rules for inputs, formulas, cross-sheet references, and totals.
limitations: Dynamic recalculation depends on LibreOffice being installed outside the skill workflow.
Manual XML edits require validation because malformed OOXML can make workbooks unreadable.
The skill does not provide live collaboration, cloud sync, or Excel add-in features.
Macro-enabled workbooks can be preserved, but the skill does not analyze VBA macro behavior.

use_cases.title: Build a Financial Model
use_cases.description: Create a workbook with formulas, assumption styling, cross-sheet links, and validation before delivery.

use_cases.title: Analyze Operational Data
use_cases.description: Read spreadsheet files, summarize sheets, inspect data quality, and produce a cleaned workbook or report.

use_cases.title: Patch Existing Workbooks
use_cases.description: Insert rows, add formula columns, and preserve workbook structure without rebuilding the file from scratch.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook named budget.xlsx with monthly revenue, cost, profit, and profit margin formulas.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Spreadsheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this spreadsheet, summarize each sheet, identify data quality issues, and report key numeric trends.

prompt_templates.title: Modify Without Format Loss
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit the existing workbook by adding a variance column, copying nearby styles, and preserving all original sheets and data.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Repair Formulas
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate all formulas, repair broken sheet references, recalculate if LibreOffice is available, and return a concise validation report.

output_examples.input: Create a quarterly revenue workbook with totals and margin percentages.
output_examples.output: A completed workbook with formula-driven totals, percentage formatting, blue input cells, and black calculated cells.

output_examples.input: Add a new expense row to an existing budget workbook.
output_examples.output: An updated workbook that preserves original sheets, shifts affected rows, updates totals, and passes formula validation.

output_examples.input: Check this workbook for formula errors before I send it.
output_examples.output: A validation summary listing checked sheets, formula counts, detected errors, and recommended fixes.

best_practices: Keep the original workbook unchanged and write edits to a new output file.
Use a dedicated temporary work directory for unpacking and repacking XLSX files.
Run formula and style validation before delivering any edited workbook.
anti_patterns: Do not recreate an existing workbook when the task asks for a targeted edit.
Do not hardcode calculated values that should be Excel formulas.
Do not install system packages or run privileged commands during a workbook task.

faq.question: Can this skill create new Excel files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses a minimal OOXML template and helper scripts to build formula-driven XLSX workbooks.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing workbook without losing formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to unpack, edit XML directly, and repack the original workbook structure.

faq.question: Does it support CSV and TSV files?
faq.answer: Yes. The reading and analysis workflow can handle CSV and TSV data for summaries and conversions.

faq.question: Does formula recalculation always work?
faq.answer: No. Dynamic recalculation only works when LibreOffice is already installed and available in the environment.

faq.question: Can it handle macro-enabled workbooks?
faq.answer: It can preserve XLSM package parts during XML edits, but it does not inspect or validate VBA macro code.

faq.question: What should users verify after edits?
faq.answer: Users should verify sheet names, sample source data, formula results, and style validation results before sharing the workbook.
